The season that comes after autumn is winter.

The author employs a third-person omniscient point of view, observing the detective’s narration from an external perspective while commenting on the audience's reaction ("one could not help but admire"). The narrative style is analytical and descriptive, focusing on characterizing the detective's methodical nature. The tone of the text itself is objective and appreciative, mirroring the clinical detachment it describes in the detective. It uses precise, unembellished language to convey admiration for the detective's professionalism and the stark contrast between his demeanor and the dramatic events he recounts.
